is-angi-worth-it.title: Is Angi Worth It for Contractors?

slides.headline: Is Angi worth it for contractors?
slides.body: The honest math most lead sites won't show you.

slides.headline: They sell the SAME lead to 5–12 of you
slides.body: Your $35 lead is really $35 × the 8 other trucks racing you to the phone.

slides.headline: Real cost per BOOKED job: $1,430–$2,500
slides.body: Once you factor the low close rates on shared leads. A job won organically? ~$290.

slides.headline: You're renting, not building
slides.body: Stop paying and the leads vanish. You bought at-bats, not an asset.

slides.headline: What to do instead
slides.body: Own your Google presence, systematize referrals, and capture the homeowners already on your site.

slides.headline: Run your own number.

slides.headline: How to price a job without leaving money on the table
slides.body: The math nobody teaches you in the apprenticeship.

slides.headline: Markup is not margin
slides.body: A 50% markup is only a 33% margin. That gap is on every job you quote, all year.

slides.headline: Know your 3 numbers
slides.body: Direct cost, overhead, and profit. You can't price what you can't see.

slides.headline: The one formula
slides.body: Price = cost ÷ (1 − target margin). A $400 job at 55% margin = $889.

slides.headline: Stop racing to the bottom
slides.body: Win the customer before it's a bidding war — then you price for margin, not survival.

slides.headline: What should you charge?
slides.body: Free margin calculator → booked-job.com/blog/how-to-price-a-job

get-more-google-reviews.title: How to Get More Google Reviews

slides.headline: How to get more Google reviews
slides.body: The cheapest marketing most shops ignore.

slides.headline: Timing beats everything
slides.body: Ask at peak gratitude — the moment the job's done and the customer's happy.

slides.headline: Make it one tap
slides.body: Text the direct review link within the hour. Don't make them search for you.

slides.headline: Ask everyone
slides.body: Only asking happy customers is 'gating' — against Google's rules. And never pay for reviews.

slides.headline: Make it a habit
slides.body: Add the ask to the end of every job + your invoice. Steady trickle beats a one-time burst.

slides.headline: The full system.
slides.body: booked-job.com/blog/get-more-google-reviews

slides.headline: Surviving the slow season
slides.body: A cash-flow playbook for the trades.

slides.headline: Win it in the busy season
slides.body: Bank a 3–6 month cushion. Sweep a fixed % of every job before it feels spendable.

slides.headline: Sell weather-proof work
slides.body: Maintenance plans, opposite-season installs, tune-ups — the highest-margin work you'll book.

slides.headline: Mine past customers
slides.body: Your cheapest pipeline isn't a lead site — it's the people who already paid you.

slides.headline: Don't go dark on marketing
slides.body: It's cheapest when competitors go quiet. Pour in then, not at peak prices.

slides.headline: The full playbook.
slides.body: booked-job.com/blog/surviving-the-slow-season

slides.headline: Cost per lead is a lie
slides.body: The only number that pays your mortgage is cost per booked JOB.

slides.headline: CPL hides the close rate
slides.body: A $35 lead you win 1-in-12 times isn't cheap — it's $420 a job before you swing a hammer.

slides.headline: Do the real math
slides.body: Angi ≈ $542 a booked job. Thumbtack ≈ $250. Google LSA ≈ $168. Same trade, wildly different truth.

slides.headline: Cheap means a bidding war
slides.body: Shared leads go to 5–12 pros. You're not buying a customer — you're buying an at-bat against 8 other trucks.

slides.headline: Track it per channel
slides.body: Ad spend ÷ jobs booked, monthly, per source. Kill what loses. Feed what wins.

slides.headline: Know your number.
slides.body: Free cost-per-job calculator → booked-job.com

slides.headline: Answer your phone.
slides.body: The cheapest marketing upgrade in the trades costs $0.

slides.headline: First to answer usually wins
slides.body: Homeowners call down the list. The first live human tends to book the job.

slides.headline: 5 minutes is the cliff
slides.body: Call back in 5 minutes vs 30 and you're up to 100× more likely to actually connect.

slides.headline: Missed call? Auto-text back
slides.body: 'Sorry we missed you — what's going on?' sent instantly saves the job.

slides.headline: Voicemail is where jobs die
slides.body: Nobody leaves one anymore. If you can't answer, forward it or use an answering service.

slides.headline: Speed wins.
slides.body: The full speed-to-lead playbook → booked-job.com

slides.headline: Your Google Business Profile is your storefront
slides.body: And most contractors leave it half-empty.

slides.headline: Fill in EVERY field
slides.body: Services, service areas, hours, description. Google ranks complete profiles over lazy ones.

slides.headline: Photos = trust + ranking
slides.body: Add job photos weekly. Fresh-photo profiles get more calls and direction requests.

slides.headline: Post like it's social
slides.body: A Google Post every week — offers, tips, finished jobs. Free space on the results page.

slides.headline: Reviews are the ranking fuel
slides.body: Steady, recent reviews with keywords ('water heater install') push you up the map pack.

slides.headline: Own the map.
slides.body: Free GBP checklist → booked-job.com

website-that-books.title: Why Your Website Doesn't Book Jobs

slides.headline: Why your website doesn't book jobs
slides.body: It looks fine. It just doesn't SELL.

slides.headline: No phone number up top
slides.body: If they have to hunt for how to reach you, they're already calling a competitor.

slides.headline: You listed services, not outcomes
slides.body: Homeowners don't want 'HVAC installation.' They want 'cool house by Friday.'

slides.headline: Zero proof
slides.body: No reviews, no photos, no faces. Trust is the whole game — put it on page one.

slides.headline: Slow = gone
slides.body: 3 seconds to load or half your visitors bounce. Speed is a booking feature.

slides.headline: Turn clicks into calls.
slides.body: Free website teardown → booked-job.com

slides.headline: Facebook or Google?
slides.body: Where a contractor's ad dollar actually works.

slides.headline: Google catches demand
slides.body: Someone typing 'emergency plumber near me' is ready to book NOW. That's the money.

slides.headline: Facebook creates demand
slides.body: Nobody scrolls Facebook needing a roof. Great for brand + big-ticket, slow for emergencies.

slides.headline: Start where the intent is
slides.body: Small budget? Google Local Service Ads first — pay per lead, badge included.

slides.headline: Then layer social
slides.body: Once the phone rings from Google, use Facebook to stay famous in your zip code.

slides.headline: Spend where it books.
slides.body: Free channel guide → booked-job.com

referrals-on-autopilot.title: A Referral Engine That Runs Itself

slides.headline: A referral engine that runs itself
slides.body: Your cheapest, highest-close pipeline — systematized.

slides.headline: Ask at the peak
slides.body: The moment the job's done and they're thrilled: 'Know anyone else who needs this?'

slides.headline: Make sharing effortless
slides.body: A card, a text link, a $25 thank-you. Remove every ounce of friction.

slides.headline: Reward BOTH sides
slides.body: Give the referrer and the new customer something. It doubles the reason to share.

slides.headline: Follow up 30 days later
slides.body: 'How's it holding up — and thanks again for any referrals.' Stay top of mind.

slides.headline: Turn jobs into more jobs.

five-numbers-to-track.title: The 5 Numbers Every Contractor Should Know

slides.headline: The 5 numbers every contractor should know
slides.body: Run the business — don't let it run you.

slides.headline: 1. Cost per booked job
slides.body: Per lead source. The only marketing number that touches your bank account.

slides.headline: 2. Close rate
slides.body: Quotes sent vs jobs won. If it's low, it's a follow-up problem, not a lead problem.

slides.headline: 3. Average job value
slides.body: Nudge it up with good/better/best options. Same trucks, bigger tickets.

slides.headline: 4. Gross margin  ·  5. Booked weeks ahead
slides.body: Margin says if it's worth it. Backlog says when to spend on marketing.

slides.headline: See your business clearly.

exclusive-vs-shared-leads.title: Why Cheap Leads Cost the Most

slides.headline: Why cheap leads cost the most
slides.body: Shared vs exclusive, in real dollars.

slides.headline: The '$35' shared lead
slides.body: Sold to 8 pros. ~1-in-8 close. Real cost per job: hundreds — plus the race to the phone.

slides.headline: The '$90' exclusive lead
slides.body: Only yours. Close ~1-in-3. Often CHEAPER per booked job than the 'cheap' one.

slides.headline: Shared leads train shoppers
slides.body: Five calls in ten minutes = a bidding war you win only on price.

slides.headline: Exclusive = a real conversation
slides.body: No competition on the line. You sell value, protect margin, book the job.

slides.headline: Price leads by BOOKED jobs.
